attrs.evidence: nest_bundle.mjs / nest_check.mjs v0.2.0, protocol TRVM-NESTED-COMPOSITION-v2 (a record-shape change is a protocol revision, per law:proof.semantic-vocabulary-closed@1). Gate `gov-nest`. MEASURED POSITIVELY rather than by refusing a negation: rewording one annotation on the P1 leaf holds 10 semantic names -- every claim id, aggregate id and certificate id at all three composition levels -- and moves 4 addresses, and the rebuilt DAG verifies. Against P4 the same edit moved all three claim ids. The grid enforces the boundary where it is enforceable: an operand carrying an artifact_root is refused nest-vocabulary-unknown, and the claim id still moves when the certificate does.
attrs.statement: A LOCATOR MAY RENAME THE ARTIFACT CARRYING A PROOF. IT MAY NOT RENAME THE PROOF. A transport or version identifier used to ACQUIRE evidence may affect the identity of the containing artifact, and may not alter the semantic identity of the claim that evidence establishes. P4 placed artifact_root inside claim.operands and therefore inside nested_claim_sem_id, so rewording one English annotation on a leaf -- non-semantic by construction, and measured to leave that leaf's verified_claim_sem_id untouched -- MOVED every ancestor's claim id, aggregate id and certificate id. The planes are separate records with separate identities: CLAIM says what is asserted, REFERENCES say where the bytes are, EVIDENCE says what holds, STRUCTURE says what shape the DAG is, and VERIFIER EXECUTION is not in the artifact at all. AND OPERATIONAL COUNTS ARE NOT PROOF SEMANTICS: how many times a checker was invoked, and whether it reused a derivation, are facts about a verification run that no artifact can be right about; putting them in the claim or the aggregate means a sound verifier changing STRATEGY renames the theorem. What an artifact may state about its own shape must be strategy-independent -- edge counts, distinct-artifact counts and byte totals are, `checker_evaluations` is not. THE SEPARATION CREATES THE ONE THING SEPARATION ALWAYS CREATES, a way for the halves to disagree, so operands and references must be matched as SETS and every citation recomputed from what was RESOLVED.
